items.text: Read the Official Eligibility Line Read the official eligibility line for each. Write it down. Cross out any path that is genuinely closed to you.

items.heading: Cbse Introduced Applied Mathematics
items.text: CBSE introduced Applied Mathematics for Classes 11 and 12 from the 2020-21 session, because standard Mathematics suits science subjects better than commerce or social-science subjects. It targets practical maths for business, finance and economics. CBSE's own advice, as reported, is that students heading for Mathematics Honours or engineering should take standard Mathematics.

rows: "B.Com (Hons) at DU is impossible without maths"

DU's 2026-27 bulletin lists a combination with Accountancy/Book Keeping instead of Mathematics for B.Com (Hons). A few coaching pages say this route was removed. The bulletin says otherwise, so check the current one.

The CFA Institute's enrolment policy asks for a completed bachelor's degree, a bachelor's programme that ends within 23 months of the Level I exam window, or 4,000 hours of work and/or higher education over at least three years. It lists no Class 12 maths condition. The exams themselves are quantitative, so it is a hard road, not a locked door.

ICAI lets you register in the Foundation after Class 10, with no stream condition. Paper 3 (Quantitative Aptitude) is real maths, so you learn it there, and graduates with 55% (commerce) or 60% (other streams) can skip the Foundation entirely.

ICSI's restructured entrance test (CSEET) has four papers: Business Communication, Fundamentals of Accounting, Economic and Business Environment, and Business Laws and Management. None is a maths or quantitative paper. Details are in the Company Secretary section below.

items.heading: Pick Two Paths
items.text: Pick two paths. For example CA and digital marketing, or BBA and a B.Com plus skill route.

items.heading: Sit One Timed Quant Section
items.text: Sit one timed quant section or sample paper. Use a public sample paper. Note which topics cost you marks, not just the score.

items.heading: Produce One Small Piece
items.text: Produce one small piece of work in each path. A one-page report, a set of practice books or a mini campaign.

items.heading: Show IT to Two People
items.text: Show it to two people who work in that field. Ask one direct question: would you pay for this or hire for this?

items.heading: "No Maths Means No Ca,
items.text: "No maths means no CA, no BBA, no MBA." Wrong on all three: CA takes any stream, most BBA programmes do not step on maths, and MBA entrances ask for a degree.

items.heading: "Take Maths Anyway, Just
items.text: "Take maths anyway, just in case." Fine if you can sustain it, costly if it damages your marks and confidence.

items.heading: "Websites List What
items.text: "Websites list what you can do, so trust the list." The popular lists contradict each other and sometimes the official documents.
